samf-junior-2010-r2-01.title: Choose the last two digits
samf-junior-2010-r2-01.body:
Write the number as $\overline{ab\,cd}$ with $\overline{ab}=2\overline{cd}$. The first two digits form a number from $10$ to $99$, so $\overline{cd}$, read as a number (possibly $05$ etc.), satisfies $10\le 2\overline{cd}\le99$, i.e. $5\le\overline{cd}\le49$. Each of these $45$ values gives exactly one number, e.g. $05\to1005$, $49\to9849$.

**Answer: (D) 45**

samf-junior-2010-r2-02.title: Isosceles triangle
samf-junior-2010-r2-02.body:
Each interior angle of a regular pentagon is $108^\circ$. Triangle $ABC$ has $AB=BC$ and $\angle B=108^\circ$, so $x=\frac{180^\circ-108^\circ}{2}=36^\circ$.

**Answer: (D) 36°**

samf-junior-2010-r2-03.title: Volume over rate
samf-junior-2010-r2-03.body:
The volume is $2\cdot2\cdot4=16\ \text{m}^3=16\,000$ litres. At $5$ litres per second this takes $3200$ s, which is $\frac{3200}{60}\approx53.3$ minutes.

**Answer: (C) 53**

samf-junior-2010-r2-04.title: Equation
samf-junior-2010-r2-04.body:
John will then have $X-4$. Let Jane have $Y$ today; then she will have $Y+4=2(X-4)$, so $Y=2X-12=2(X-6)$.

**Answer: (D) $2(X-6)$**

samf-junior-2010-r2-05.title: Rearrange and add
samf-junior-2010-r2-05.body:
The first equation gives $a+d=c-b$ and the second gives $a+d=b-c$. Adding: $2(a+d)=0$, so $a+d=0$.

**Answer: (D) 0**

samf-junior-2010-r2-06.title: Let Bernard be x
samf-junior-2010-r2-06.body:
Bernard is $x$, Charlie $x+4$, Arthur $\frac{x+4}2$. In six years the sum is $(x+6)+(x+10)+\left(\frac{x+4}{2}+6\right)=\frac52x+24=69$, so $x=18$.

**Answer: (C) 18**

samf-junior-2010-r2-06.title: Check the answer
samf-junior-2010-r2-06.body:
Bernard $18$, Charlie $22$, Arthur $11$. In six years: $24+28+17=69$. ✓

**Answer: (C) 18**

samf-junior-2010-r2-07.title: Use the lcm
samf-junior-2010-r2-07.body:
A number leaves remainder $1$ on division by both $21$ and $35$ exactly when $n-1$ is a multiple of $\operatorname{lcm}(21,35)=105$. So $n=1,106,211,\dots$, i.e. $n=1+105k$ with $1+105k<1000$, so $k=0,1,\dots,9$: ten numbers.

**Answer: (C) 10**

samf-junior-2010-r2-08.title: Take 40 pupils
samf-junior-2010-r2-08.body:
Out of every $40$ pupils, $25$ are seniors and $15$ juniors. Of the $15$ juniors, $9$ are boys and $6$ girls; of the $25$ seniors, $10$ are boys and $15$ girls. Boys: $9+10=19$; girls: $6+15=21$. The ratio is $19:21$.

**Answer: (A) 19 : 21**

samf-junior-2010-r2-09.title: Speed ratio
samf-junior-2010-r2-09.body:
For the same distance, one third of the time means three times the speed. So John's speed is $3x$ if Dave's is $x$, and $3x=x+10$, giving $x=5$.

**Answer: (B) 5**

samf-junior-2010-r2-11.title: Add in pairs from the second term
samf-junior-2010-r2-11.body:
From the second term on: $(-4+9)+(-16+25)+\dots+(-576+625)=5+9+13+\dots+49$, with $12$ terms; together with the first term $1$ we get $1+5+9+\dots+49$: $13$ terms with average $25$, total $13\cdot25=325$.

**Answer: (E) 325**

samf-junior-2010-r2-12.title: Count the choices per digit
samf-junior-2010-r2-12.body:
First digit: $1,3,5,7,9$ ($5$ choices). Second digit: $2,5,8$ ($3$). Third digit: $3,7$ ($2$). Fourth digit: $4,9$ ($2$). Total $5\cdot3\cdot2\cdot2=60$. (The first digit is never $0$, so all are four-digit numbers.)

**Answer: (B) 60**

samf-junior-2010-r2-13.title: Use the height from M
samf-junior-2010-r2-13.body:
$M$ is the centre of the square, so its distance to side $BC$ is $\frac12$. Triangle $BMP$ has base $BP$ on $BC$ and height $\frac12$, so its area is $\frac12\cdot BP\cdot\frac12=\frac{BP}4$. Setting $\frac{BP}{4}=\frac15$ gives $BP=\frac45$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac45$**

samf-junior-2010-r2-14.title: Subtract a small triangle
samf-junior-2010-r2-14.body:
By symmetry about $O$, $DP=x$, so $PC=3-x$. The shaded region is triangle $ADC$ (area $\frac92$) without triangle $POC$. Triangle $POC$ has base $PC=3-x$ and height $\frac32$ (the distance from $O$ to $DC$), so its area is $\frac34(3-x)$. Shaded area $=\frac92-\frac34(3-x)=\frac{9+3x}{4}=\frac34(x+3)$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac34(x+3)$**

samf-junior-2010-r2-14.title: Test extreme positions
samf-junior-2010-r2-14.body:
If $x=0$, then $Q=B$, $P=D$ and the shaded region is triangle $AOD$, a quarter of the square: $\frac94$. If $x=3$, then $Q=A$, $P=C$ and the shaded region is triangle $ADC$: $\frac92$. Option (C) gives $\frac94$ and $\frac92$; (A) gives $\frac94$ and $3$, (B) gives $\frac32$ at $x=0$, (D) gives $\frac{45}4$ at $x=0$, and (E) gives $\frac94$ and $\frac9{16}$. Only (C) fits both.

**Answer: (C)**

samf-junior-2010-r2-15.title: Along the diagonal
samf-junior-2010-r2-15.body:
The big circle has radius $1$ and centre at the centre of the square, at distance $\sqrt2$ from the corner. The small circle of radius $r$ touches both sides at the corner, so its centre is at distance $r\sqrt2$ from the corner, and it touches the big circle externally, so the distance between the centres is $1+r$. Along the diagonal: $\sqrt2=r\sqrt2+r+1$, so $r=\frac{\sqrt2-1}{\sqrt2+1}$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{\sqrt2-1}{\sqrt2+1}$**

samf-junior-2010-r2-16.title: Compute the volumes
samf-junior-2010-r2-16.body:
At the start: $900$ cm$^3$ water and $100$ cm$^3$ oil. Afterwards: $450$ cm$^3$ water and $100$ cm$^3$ oil, total $550$. The percentage of water is $\frac{450}{550}=\frac9{11}\approx81.8\%$, which is closest to $82\%$.

**Answer: (A) 82%**

samf-junior-2010-r2-17.title: Small triangle on top
samf-junior-2010-r2-17.body:
The part of the triangle above the square is a small equilateral triangle whose base is the top side of the square, so its side $b$ equals the square's side $s$. Below it, the left side of the big triangle runs a vertical distance $s$ along the square, so $a$ is the hypotenuse of a $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle with the vertical leg $s$: $a=\frac{s}{\sin60^\circ}=\frac{2s}{\sqrt3}$. Hence $\frac ab=\frac2{\sqrt3}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{2}{\sqrt3}$**

samf-junior-2010-r2-18.title: Compare areas
samf-junior-2010-r2-18.body:
The small circles have radius $1$ (area $\pi$ each). Each adjacent pair of small circles overlaps in a lens of area $y$ (the cross-hatched part), and opposite circles only touch. Let $x$ be the area of one of the four gaps between the large circle and two neighbouring small circles (the hatched part). The big circle (area $4\pi$) is the union of the four small circles plus the four gaps: $4\pi=(4\pi-4y)+4x$. So $x=y$ and the difference is $0$.

**Answer: (E) 0**

samf-junior-2010-r2-19.title: Same parity
samf-junior-2010-r2-19.body:
The sum is even exactly when both numbers are even or both odd. The number of pairs: $\binom82=28$. Both even: $\binom42=6$; both odd: $\binom42=6$. Probability $\frac{12}{28}=\frac37$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac37$**

samf-junior-2010-r2-19.title: Condition on the first card
samf-junior-2010-r2-19.body:
Whatever the first card is, $3$ of the remaining $7$ cards have the same parity as it. So the probability is $\frac37$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac37$**

samf-junior-2010-r2-20.title: Logic
samf-junior-2010-r2-20.body:
The three sports are soccer, cricket and rugby, each played by exactly one of the boys. Suppose Adam plays soccer or cricket. By (3), Chris does not play rugby; by (4), Bob does not play rugby either; then nobody plays rugby, a contradiction. So Adam plays rugby. Then Bob does not play soccer (otherwise Adam would play cricket by (1)), so Bob plays cricket and Chris plays soccer. This is consistent with all four statements, and only (C) is correct.

**Answer: (C) Adam plays rugby**
